sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
### 1.1 Purpose
This document defines the software requirements for the Hospital EMR Patient Management System (Patient Portal). It serves as the baseline for design, implementation, and verification of the system.

### 1.2 Scope
The system provides a secure interface for patients to interact with their Electronic Medical Records (EMR) managed by the hospital. The scope encompasses patient authentication, record viewing, and secure data transmission.

### 1.3 Definitions
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record.
- **PHI**: Protected Health Information.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body: The Patient Portal operates as a web-based application integrated with the Hospital EMR backend. The architecture consists of a presentation layer (UI), an application layer (business logic and API gateway), and a data layer (EMR database). All data flows between the portal and the EMR must be encrypted in transit. The system is designed to handle concurrent patient sessions while maintaining strict data isolation per user.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: System shall support secure login via username and password with multi-factor authentication (MFA) capability.
System shall allow authenticated patients to view their medical history, lab results, and appointment schedules.
System shall encrypt all data in transit between the client and server using TLS 1.2 or higher.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements (Performance, Security, Reliability mapped to domain standards)
sections.body:
### 4.1 Performance
- **NFR-001**: The system shall achieve a P95 latency of < 250ms for standard page loads and API responses, per healthcare domain benchmarks.

### 4.2 Security (HIPAA Compliance)
- **NFR-002 (Encryption at Rest)**: Per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv), the system shall implement encryption for all Protected Health Information (PHI) stored at rest. AES-256 or equivalent standard shall be used for database encryption.
- **NFR-003 (Audit Logging)**: Per HIPAA §164.312(b), the system shall implement an audit control mechanism that records and examines activity in information systems that contain PHI. All access, modification, and deletion events involving PHI must be logged with user ID, timestamp, and action type.

### 4.3 Reliability
- **NFR-004**: The system shall maintain 99.9% availability during business hours.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements (APIs, UI, Hardware)
sections.body:
### 5.1 User Interface
The system shall provide a responsive web interface accessible via standard browsers. The UI must clearly display patient data with appropriate masking for sensitive fields where required.

### 5.2 External APIs
The system shall integrate with the Hospital EMR backend via secure RESTful APIs. All API endpoints must enforce OAuth 2.0 for authorization.

### 5.3 Hardware
No specific hardware constraints are defined in the source document; standard cloud infrastructure is assumed.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
### 6.1 Constraints
- The system must comply with all applicable HIPAA Security Rule provisions.
- Data residency must remain within the hospital's designated geographic region (specific region not defined in source; open item).

### 6.2 Compliance Verification
- **HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv)**: Verified via NFR-002 (Encryption at Rest).
- **HIPAA §164.312(b)**: Verified via NFR-003 (Audit Logging).
- **Performance Benchmark**: Verified via NFR-001 (P95 < 250ms).

*Note: The source document is minimal. Specifics regarding data residency, backup frequency, and disaster recovery procedures are missing and require stakeholder input.*
